explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/442: if A ⊆ ℕ has (1/log log x) Σ_{n∈A, n<x} 1/n → ∞, must (Σ_{n∈A, n<x} 1/n)^{-2} Σ_{a<b in A∩(1,x]} 1/lcm(a,b) → ∞? Tao [Ta24b] showed this is false. The statement negates the universal implication, using Log x = max(log x, 1) (following Tao's paper, harmless for large x), sums over A ∩ [1, ⌊x⌋], and pairs n < m in that range. Small range differences are immaterial: including the endpoint x and allowing n = 1 in the pair sum adds at most S = Σ 1/n to the pair sum, which contributes only 1/S → 0 after dividing by S². Faithful; a Lean proof is linked.
